tagline: From Sandhills to river farmland, with a Danish village along the way
intro: Nebraska’s Loup Rivers Scenic Byway runs 150 miles on Highways 91 and 11 between Dunning and Wood River. The Nebraska Department of Transportation includes it among the state’s two-lane scenic routes. Visit Nebraska highlights rolling farmland, winding rivers, red barns and silos, with the Sandhills and Calamus River among the landscape’s contrasts. Dunning stands where the Dismal River meets the Middle Loup. Farther along, Highway 11 parallels the North Loup between Burwell and Elba. Near Burwell, the Calamus River feeds Calamus Reservoir State Recreation Area, another waterway along the journey.

Rail connections changed several towns along the present corridor. Wood River moved to follow its railroad depot in 1874. North Loup’s rail connection arrived in 1882 and brought a boom that ended when the line reached Ord in 1886. The Ord line continues to carry agricultural produce from Valley County.

From Dunning, take Highway 91 northeast through the Sandhills, past the junction south of Brewster, then east and southeast into farmland toward Taylor. At Burwell, the journey turns to Highway 11, which parallels the North Loup River toward Ord and Elba. Continue through Dannebrog and Cairo to Wood River, leaving the North Loup stretch for the southern farm miles.
notice: Red barns and silos mark the farmland along the byway.

moments.title: Fort Hartsuff
moments.text: Fort Hartsuff served as a U.S. Army cavalry outpost from 1874 to 1881. The state historical park lies six miles southeast of Burwell. Its surviving original buildings include the headquarters, enlisted men’s barracks, officers’ quarters, commanding officer’s quarters and hospital. Other buildings are reconstructions.
moments.notice: Original buildings include the headquarters, enlisted men’s barracks, officers’ quarters and hospital; other buildings are reconstructed.

moments.title: Ord
moments.text: Ord’s railway still carries agricultural produce, continuing a transport connection established in 1886. The Omaha and Republican Valley Railway built the 59-mile line from Grand Island under the Union Pacific Railroad. Nebraska Central Railroad now serves the line, which connects with Union Pacific’s national system. The line’s arrival in Ord ended a boom in North Loup, which had gained its own rail connection in 1882. At the Valley County Museum, another kind of travel has a local story: Evelyn Sharp, who became the country’s youngest female commercial pilot after turning 18 in the 1930s.

moments.title: Dannebrog
moments.text: Dannebrog carries the Danish name for Denmark’s flag. A colony of Danes from Milwaukee established the settlement in 1871, and the railroad reached it in 1886. In 1908, the Danish Brotherhood in America built Columbia Hall as a meeting place for the Danish community. Columbia Hall entered the National Register of Historic Places in 2005. The building now houses a tourist center and an archive of Danish American history. The village also celebrates Danish heritage at Grundlovsfest on the first weekend in June.
